Date: 2023-02-24
REMARKS
Applicant replies to the non-final Office Action dated November 28, 2022, in which this Reply is filed within three months. Claims 1-9, 11-12, and 14-21 stand rejected. Dependent claim 16 is currently amended. Support for the amendment can be found in the originally-filed specification, claims, and figures. No new matter is entered with this amendment. Reconsideration is respectfully requested.
Claim Objections
Claim 16 is objected to as depending from a cancelled claim 15. Applicant amends claim 16 herein to obviate the objection. Applicant respectfully requests the objection be withdrawn in light of the amendment.
Rejections under 102
Claims 1-5, 7, 8, 11, 16, and 22 are rejected under 102 as being anticipated by O'Brien (U.S. Patent Publ. No. 2018/0018519). Applicant traverses the rejection.
The standard for anticipation under 35 USC 102 is that every aspect of a claim must identically appear in a single reference for it to anticipate the claim under 35 USC 102 (In re Bond, 15 USPQ2d 1566 (Fed. Cir. 1990)). "A claim is anticipated only if each and every element as set forth in the claim is found, either expressly or inherently described, in a single prior art reference." Verdegaal Bros v. Union Oil Co. of California, 814 F.2d 628, 631 (Fed. Cir. 1987). "The identical invention must be shown in as complete detail as is contained in the ... claim." Richardson v. Suzuki Motor Co., 868 F.2d 1226, 1236 (Fed. Cir. 1989).
O'Brien Fails to Disclose "the First Cargo Handling Robot and the Second Cargo Handling Robot Are Configured to Simultaneously Couple to a Common Cargo Unit" As Claimed The Office Action asserts on pages 2-3 that O'Brien discloses "the first cargo handling robot and the second cargo handling robot are configured to simultaneously couple to a common cargo unit (paragraph 16) to transport the cargo unit from a first position on a cargo deck (not numbered, but shown in fig. 1; Note: the surface the robots seat on is the cargo deck) to a different second position on the cargo deck (paragraph 19)." (Emphasis added). Applicant disagrees.
Applicant submits that the Office has failed to demonstrate that O'Brien discloses the autonomous robot pickers 108a-b are simultaneously coupled to the physical object taught by O'Brien. ¶[0016] of O'Brien provides no disclosure or contemplation of the autonomous robot pickers 108a and 108b configured to simultaneously couple to a common cargo unit to transport the cargo unit from a first position on a cargo deck to a different second position on the cargo deck, as claimed. In stark contrast, O'Brien teaches in ¶[0016] transporting the packaged physical object to a first station with the conveyor belt 100, which can include the autonomous robot picker 108a to unpack the physical object from the packaging. After being unpacked, the conveyor belt 100 transports the unpacked physical object to the station including the reader(s) 110 (see ¶[0018] of O'Brien), then to the station including the X-ray machine 120 (see ¶[0019] of O'Brien), and then to the end of the conveyor belt 100 where the autonomous robot picker 108b can remove the package from the conveyor belt 100 (see ¶[0019] of O'Brien).
In this regard, not only does O'Brien fail to disclose simultaneously coupling the autonomous robot pickers 108a and 108b to the package, O'Brien is limited to a system wherein the autonomous robot picker 108a and autonomous robot picker 108b are configured for completely separate tasks (i.e., autonomous robot picker 108a configured to detect and unpackage the physical object 118 (see ¶[0016] and [0019] of O'Brien) and autonomous robot picker 108b is configured to place and/or remove the physical object 118 from the conveyer belt 100 (see ¶[0019] of O'Brien).
For all the foregoing reasons, Applicant submits that the Office has failed to demonstrate that O'Brien discloses at least "the first cargo handling robot and the second cargo handling robot are configured to simultaneously couple to a common cargo unit" as claimed.
Therefore, O'Brien does not anticipate Applicant's claims 1 and 11.
O'Brien Fails to Disclose "the First Cargo Handling Robot and the Second Cargo Handling Robot Comprise a Sensing Agent Comprising a Sensing Module, a Computing Module, and a Communication Module" As Claimed
The Office Action asserts on page 3 that O'Brien discloses "the first cargo handling robot and the second cargo handling robot comprise a sensing agent comprising a sensing module (104), a computing module (200), and a communication module (paragraph 26)." (Emphasis added). Applicant disagrees.
O'Brien recites, "The physical object assessment system 112 includes a conveyer belt 100, a scale 102, image capturing device(s) 104, a reader(s) 110, autonomous robot pickers 108 a-b and an x-ray machine 120." (O'Brien, ¶[0015]). O'Brien further recites, "The image capturing device 104, the scale 102, the autonomous robot picker 108 a, the reader 110, and x-ray machine 120 can be disposed at stations positioned at different locations along the length of the conveyor belt 100." Thus, O'Brien's image capturing device 104 is completely separate from O'Brien's autonomous robot picker 108a. Applicant submits that the Office has failed to demonstrate that O'Brien's autonomous robot picker 108a or autonomous robot picker 108b comprises Obrien's image capturing device 104. Applicant submits that the Office has failed to demonstrate that O'Brien discloses "the first cargo handling robot and the second cargo handling robot comprise a sensing agent comprising a sensing module," as claimed.
For similar reasons as discussed above with respect to O'Brien's image capturing device 104, Applicant submits the Office fails to demonstrate that O'Brien's autonomous robot picker 108a or autonomous robot picker 108b comprises Obrien's-computing system 200 and/or Obrien's "communication module (paragraph 26).
Therefore, O'Brien does not anticipate Applicant's claims 1 and 11.
Improper Reliance on One Element in Reference to Read on Two Claimed Elements Applicant's claimed "control module" and "computing module" are recited as different limitations, and therefore, are different components of Applicant's claimed invention. The Examiner cannot rely on one element in a reference (computing system 200 of O'Brien) to read onto two of Applicant's claimed elements (the computing module and the control module). Ex parte Weideman, No. 2008-003454; App. No.10/035,334, slip op. 7 (BPAI Jan. 27, 2009) ("Consistent with the principle that all limitations in a claim must be considered to be meaningful, it is improper to rely on the same structure in the Lohr reference as being responsive to two different elements (seat bottom and center support) in claim 1"); see also In re Robertson, 169 F.3d 743, 745 (Claims requiring three separate means cannot be anticipated by structure that contains only two means using one element twice); Lantech Inc. v. Keip Machine Co., 32 F.3d 542, 547 (Fed. Cir. 1994). Therefore, the Examiner's reliance on computing system 200 of O'Brien to anticipate both Applicant's computing module and control module is improper. O'Brien does not disclose or contemplate a control module and a computing module, and therefore, O'Brien does not anticipate Applicant's claims 1 and 11.
For all the foregoing reasons, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the 102 rejection of claims 1 and 11.
Rejections under 103
Claims 17-21 are rejected under 103 as being unpatentable over O'Brien. Applicant traverses the rejection.
Regarding claim 17, the Office Action merely recites:
Claims 17-21 is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentableover O'Brlen etal.
Regarding claims 17-21, the recited method steps for moving a cargo unit is considered to be obvious to O'Brien et al., since O'Brien et al. discloses all of the structural Lmitations in the claims as discussed above.
It would have been obvious to one having ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the invention to have performed theclaimed method by the apparatusof O'Brienetal. for the purpose of providing an efficient means of moving a packaged physlcal object from one place to a not her.
Claim 17 recites the following limitations not disclosed by O'Brien for the same reasons discussed above with respect to claims 1 and 11.
* "attaching the first cargo handling robot and the second cargo handling robot to the cargo unit at the first position" and "moving, via the first cargo handling robot and the second cargo handling robot, the cargo unit to the second position, wherein the first cargo handling robot and the second cargo handling robot transport the cargo unit horizontally about a cargo deck in response to moving from the first position to the second position;" and
* "wherein the first cargo handling robot and the second cargo handling robot comprise a sensing agent comprising a sensing module, a computing module, and a communication module."
Applicant submits the comments above with respect to claims 1 and 11 apply, mutatis mutandis, to independent claim 17. Accordingly, none of the cited references disclose or even contemplate these features, and thus Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of this rejection of claim 17.
Based upon the foregoing, claims 1, 11, and 17 are allowable over O'Brien. All claims that depend from claim 1, 11, or 17 are thereby also allowable over O'Brien for the above-noted reasons. There is therefore no need to separately address the patentability of each of these claims and/or the Patent Office's interpretation in relation to any of these claims or any of the references of record in relation thereto.
Further, because the Office Action failed to establish a prima facie case of anticipation, any rejection in a subsequent Office Action providing adequate reasoning(s) would be presented for the first time on the record, and, as such, a subsequent Office Action cannot be made final.
CONCLUSION
In view of the above remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that all pending claims are allowable and requests allowance of the pending claims. The Examiner is invited to telephone the undersigned at the Examiner's convenience, if that would help further prosecution of the subject application. Applicant authorizes and respectfully request that any fees due or overpayments be charged or credited to Deposit Account No. 19-2814. This statement does NOT authorize payment of the issue fee.
